header: Reason the study is a digital model
rows: Rain concentration and sheltering effect of solar panels on cultivated plots

AVrain is a validated physics-based model, but it was run offline in R on recorded event data, and the panel avoidance strategy was a wind-direction rule with no model in the loop. The claim that it 'allows real-time strategies' is a potential use that the paper neither designs as an architecture nor runs.
Optimizing Light Environment of the Oblique Single-axis Tracking Agrivoltaic System

The light model is a pure simulation of a hypothetical site. The proposed tracking algorithm is a rule based on sun-position geometry and light-saturation thresholds, applied only in simulation for one day, with no model in the loop and no hardware.
A Photovoltaic Greenhouse with Variable Shading for the Optimization of Agricultural and Energy Production

A simple radiation and shading simulation for clear-sky days on the 15th of each month estimates internal radiation for given shading percentages, with no automated input from the prototype. Panels are rotated to keep internal radiation at a set limit (e.g., 400 W m-2), which is rule-based shading control rather than model-driven actuation; the light model is simple enough that it could also be read as borderline.
Analysis of the Day-ahead Deviation Plan and Research on the Real-time Scheduling of Photovoltaic Greenhouses Based on Exergy Theory

A physics-based thermal and exergy model plus an optimization scheduler is evaluated as a calculation case study using greenhouse data. The text describes no software data link from the installation and no automatic execution of the plans on storage or loads.
MODELLING AND MEASUREMENT OF A PHOTOVOLTAIC CELL ARRAY MAXIMUM POWER POINT TRACKING SYSTEM FOR GREENHOUSE
A PV power simulation is used offline to tune a fuzzy MPPT controller. The real-time converter control is rule-based and has no model with live input in the loop.
RESEARCH ON MAXIMUM POWER POINT TRACKING’S ALGORITHM OF PHOTO-VOLTAIC CELL ARRAY FOR GREENHOUSE
An offline Simulink PV/MPPT model is used to evaluate a rule-based incremental-conductance MPPT algorithm, and a circuit test was run. No installation data feed the model.
Design and Simulation of Smart Greenhouse for Agrivoltaics Microclimates Optimization
A design-stage CFD microclimate simulation is the only virtual model. IoT monitoring goes to a smartphone display, and the fan and ventilation control appears range-based.
Development of a quick-scan webtool to facilitate agrivoltaic system design*
The webtool runs pre-computed simulations from typical-year weather data and user-set geometry. It has no link to any specific installation and gives outputs only to people as design guidance.
A Decision Support Software Application for the Design of Agrophotovoltaic Systems in Republic of Korea

The regression models were calibrated once on historical field-trial data and are used in a planning and supply-chain DSS that has no streaming input from an installation. Its outputs are design recommendations for people, not actuation.
Design & Analysis of Smart Agrivoltaic Monitoring System: Bangladesh Perspective
An offline sizing simulation gives a digital model, and the irrigation switches on directly from sensor data with no model in the loop. Neither element makes it a shadow or twin.
Performance evaluation of vertical bifacial and single-axis tracked agrivoltaic systems on arable land
A Concept of Smart Agro-Photovoltaic Tunnels

A photosynthesis model and energy/water balance analyses are used to set solar-underexposure thresholds and a proposed control method. The packet is cut off before the control-algorithm chapters, so whether the model runs in a live loop is unclear, and the lower level is chosen.
Agricultural friendly single-axis dynamic agrivoltaics: Simulations, experiments and a large-scale application for Chinese solar greenhouses
Simulations of the tracking strategies form an offline digital model. The trackers follow predefined strategies and seasonal mode switches, with no automated installation data feeding a model.
Agrovoltaic systems for crop improvement in Equatorial Andean Regions
PV yield is estimated with PVGIS for sizing; irrigation on the prototype runs on a fixed timer, not from a model.
Design and development of a graphical interface to determine the appropriate transparency level of solar greenhouse covers in Mexico
A design-support interface runs a simplified agrivoltaic model on crop and location inputs. 'Real-time' refers to computation speed, not live installation data.
Development of artificial lighting system for light supplementation in smart greenhouses with agrivoltaic systems

The lighting design (DiaLux) and the consumption-estimation regression are offline models fed with typical-year and archive weather data, not with live data from the greenhouses. The lamps are switched by fuzzy-logic rules on measured luminosity with no virtual model in the loop, so this is a digital model alongside sensor/rule-based control. The packet is the SSRN preprint, not the published version.
Influence of the Albedo on Agrivoltaics Electricity Production

The ray-tracing simulations use EPW weather files. Measured data go to a cloud database and are converted to yield afterwards with PVWatts, and no automated model ingestion is described. Tracker motion comes from a conventional PLC rule, with no model in the loop.
Modelling Canopy Temperature of Crops With Heterogeneous Canopies Grown Under Solar Panels

The model is meant to steer the panels, but the text never says how the AVD sensor data reach it, and its outputs are also described as passed to the grower. Following the protocol, the lower level is coded. The only results are a comparison with hand-held IR thermometer readings and simulations on historical 2019 data.
Rooftop greenhouse system based on photovoltaic and Internet of Things research and design

A GWO-BP temperature forecaster exists, but it is evaluated only in MATLAB simulation, and the abstract does not say the LoRa/NB-IoT monitoring data feed it. The fuzzy-PID temperature control is feedback/rule control with no virtual model in the loop.
Experimental development and numerical modeling of energy system performance in smart greenhouses with agrivoltaic systems in low-latitude regions

The greenhouses are operating, and their lighting and heating are switched by an expert-rule fuzzy-logic controller acting on sensor set points, with no virtual model in the loop. The energy models were used for design and for offline analysis of logged data under hypothetical set points, so the study is a digital_model.
Fast ground irradiance computations for agrivoltaics via physics-informed deep learning models

A deep-learning surrogate of raytraced ground irradiance was trained and tested on public historical weather data and simulated maps of the Morschenich-Alt geometry. Use in tracker control at the edge is only mentioned as a future possibility, with no live data link and no actuation.
Hybrid cooling for a strawberry photovoltaic greenhouse and energy evaluation
A physics-based cooling-load and energy model is analysed with PID/PI controllers, apparently in simulation. No automated installation data or model-driven actuation is reported.
Multi-objective optimization of photovoltaic greenhouses with modelling and field validation

Adjudicated for consistency with the rule applied to R1384: the multi-objective model is run offline to build a lookup table, and during operation the controller selects set-points from that table; no installation data reach the model and the model does not act on the installation, so the designed level is a digital model.
Next-Generation Water Management and Crop Modeling of Sustainable Energy in PLC Based on Agrivoltaics Systems With IoT

The PLC and LoRaWAN irrigation runs on sensor thresholds and user-set rules. The optimization and crop models are run in MATLAB simulation, and the text never shows field data reaching them automatically. The packet stops partway through, before the crop-modelling and results sections, which could show a live model input (digital_shadow).
Power Electronics and Control for an off-Grid Agrivoltaic Irrigation System

The PV and irrigation power system is modelled and tested in simulation, which makes it a digital model. MPPT and irrigation control are feedback controllers, and a simulated loop is not a demonstration.
Sustainable greenhouse microclimate modeling: A comparative analysis of recurrent and Graph Neural Networks

Data-driven microclimate models are trained and tested offline on historical greenhouse datasets that went through manual imputation, train/test splits and normalisation. The digital twin is mentioned only as a future goal, with no automated ingestion or actuation.
An integrated IoT-based decision-support platform for agrivoltaic systems: Design, implementation and pilot-scale field evaluation

Sensor data reach the cloud platform automatically, but the full text does not show a model receiving them: the irrigation module is described as field-data-based and was assessed retrospectively, so under the rule for unclear evidence the lower level is coded.
Artificial Intelligence-Based Optimal Energy and Water Management System in Agrivoltaics
CNN-Assisted Growth Monitoring and Stress Management of Cucumber in Semi-Transparent PV Greenhouses for Agrivoltaics

The only model of system behavior is a PV energy simulation driven by simulated irradiance; the CNN segmentation and stress classification are perception, not models of system behavior, and shading and irrigation run on sensor set-points.
Co-optimization Method for Agri-PV Systems Considering Dynamic Shading and Power Generation Performance

The shadow and PV power models support design optimization of tilt and spacing. The abstract mentions real-time meteorological data but does not say they come automatically from a specific installation, so digital_model is assigned.
Controlling PV Panels Tilt Orientation for Optimal Crop Shading and Power Generation in Agrivoltaics

An optimization model is designed to set tilt automatically, but it is evaluated only in numerical simulations using plant data, with no automated link to the installation. With no automated input, the level is digital_model.
Data-driven Analysis of Crop Yield in a Controlled Agrivoltaic Installation
Monitoring and assessment of elevated agrivoltaic systems in southern Spain

Shading and PV simulation models are run offline and compared with monitoring data; the automatic datalogger upload goes to cloud storage, and nothing in the text says it feeds the models. Panel tilt is adjusted manually, so there is no model-driven actuation.
Novel Operational Strategies to Maximize Crop and Electricity Production in Single Axis Agrivoltaic Systems Based on Light Response Curve and Daily Light Integral

The crop-informed tracking strategies are evaluated only in simulation, driven by historical 2019 SMHI weather data with no live link to the Karrbo tracker. Under the protocol, simulated closed-loop tilt control is not actuation.
Optimizing energy supply-demand in photovoltaic greenhouses: A three-layer framework informed by the crop production calendar

Measured hourly load and PV data from one year are analysed offline with a battery model and an optimization, with no live data link and no actuation by the model. The greenhouse's existing set-point HVAC controller is background, not part of the studied system. The packet is the preprint ("The critical mismatch..."), which lacks the published version's three-layer framework with real-time control, so the published text could plausibly change the designed level.
Performance evaluation of a dynamic tracking photovoltaic greenhouse system

Shading, irradiance, thermal and power models were built and checked offline against data from an experimental tracking PV greenhouse, but no software link feeds the models from the installation, despite the 'real-time model' wording. The trackers follow a time-based sun-position algorithm with PID motor control, not model outputs.
Smart Agrivoltaics for Precision Agriculture: a Sustainable Simulation-Driven Architecture

The simulation models are calibrated offline on historical nursery data, real-time data assimilation is named only as future work, and the tilt control engine seems to act on sensor data rather than on model outputs. The 'digital twin environment' claim is not backed by the text, so the lower level applies, and the agrivoltaic layer is still in design with nothing run on hardware.
Study on indoor thermal environment and photovoltaic income of a BIPV greenhouse

Sensor monitoring and an environmental control system run in experimental greenhouses, while PVsyst is used offline for energy and economic assessment. The model has no automated input, so the level is digital_model.

Solar hybrid tracking system under complex weather conditions and control criterion; [复杂天气状况下的太阳能混合跟踪系统及控制判据]

Raspberry Pi/Arduino hybrid solar tracker with weather-threshold control, tested on a small PV prototype. PV agriculture is cited only as a possible application, and there is no crop or agricultural production. Control is by threshold rules, not by a model of an installation.
CFD simulation study on module layout of photovoltaic greenhouse; [光伏温室大棚组件布置CFD模拟研究]

A transient CFD model of a PV greenhouse, driven by hourly temperature and radiation, simulates air and soil temperature and soil-surface irradiance for different module layouts. The 50% coverage option is chosen against crop light and temperature needs. Design simulation only.
Impact of Agricultural Photovoltaic on the Farm Household Income; [영농형 태양광 설치에 따른 농가소득 영향분석]
Farm household income calculation model for agricultural PV in Korea under different subsidy assumptions. Economic only.
Suitability screening of soybean varieties at seedling stage under photovoltaic panels; [光伏板下不同大豆品种苗期适宜性筛选]

Seedling-stage screening of 31 soybean varieties under PV panels in a Zhejiang solar greenhouse. PCA, a membership function and cluster analysis rank shade tolerance from measured traits. This is an agronomic trial with standard multivariate statistics and no model of system behavior (borderline).

The development of agricultural use in the area of the photovoltaic power plant D3 next to the flow accumulation of the HE Brežice; [Razvoj kmetijske rabe na območju fotovoltaične elektrarne D3 ob pretočni akumulaciji HE Brežice]
Planning study for agricultural use (species selection, costs and revenues) at an existing 8.8 ha Slovenian PV plant. No model, AI or data system.
Effect of dual-channel red/blue optical filter on the growth of plants
Pot experiment in a glass greenhouse on a red/blue optical filter and lettuce, cucumber and water spinach growth. It reports measured outcomes only, with no PV energy or modeling component.
Dynamic modeling and control of cleaning robot for agro-photovoltaic

Kinematic/kinetic modeling and controller design for a panel-cleaning robot carrier in solar farms (MATLAB-ADAMS co-simulation). The abstract describes solar farms with no agricultural production, and robot dynamics is not a model of agrivoltaic system behavior. Simulation only, not linked to live data.

The Administrative Court of Puglia rules on agrivoltaic plants: is it possible for renewable energy and agricultural production to coexist?; [Il Tar Lecce si pronuncia sugli impianti agrivoltaici: è possibile far coesistere fonti rinnovabili e produzione agricola?]
Commentary on a ruling by the Puglia administrative court on agrivoltaic plants. Legal analysis, not primary research.
Principle and modeling analysis of an agro-photovoltaic system using filter film and light reflection; [利 用 滤 光 膜 和 反 光 作 用 的 新 型 农 光 互 补 方 阵原理与建模分析]

Agro-PV array design using a spectral filter film that reflects red/blue light to the crops, with array layout and spacing designed. One-year follow-up of grass growth and sheep performance under PV at Verneuil, Nièvre (France). Monitoring results only, with no model or dedicated data system. Possibly a short report.
Allocation and Challenges of Photovoltaic Power Generation Capacity into Municipalities to Realize Carbon-neutral; [カーボンニュートラルに必要な太陽光発電の市区町村への配分とその課題]
Allocation of PV capacity potential across municipalities in Japan's Chubu region, with solar sharing as one category. A regional potential assessment with no specific system.

Topic modeling of YouTube posts and comments on rural solar power in Korea. A social-opinion and perception study, with no AI applied to an agrivoltaic system.

Field trial of saladette tomato under PV panels at three tilt angles against a control in semi-arid Arequipa, Peru. Reports measured growth and yield only, with no model or data system. The site is semi-arid/desert.

Stand-alone PV system (14.72 kW, battery, data measurement and collection system) powering a crop greenhouse at KACST al-Muzahmyah, Saudi Arabia. rows: I1: is the grassland under the array 'crops or pasture' or natural vegetation? E2: does the study build a model or sensing system, or only measure outcomes?

Methods, Site (p. 5): "Underneath the panels is a near monodominant patch of smooth brome (Bromus inermis), a common C3 pasture grass. [...] Prior to the solar array installation, this land was a hay farm for 50 years, consisting primarily of Bromus inermis." | Results and discussion (p. 3): "by simulating an AV system with a between-panel spacing of 6 m (an approximate average width of commonly used harvesters) we estimate reductions in scaled whole-AV ET of 4.5% and a negligible decrease in carbon uptake of 0.6%."

I1 is met: the vegetation is a near-monoculture of an introduced pasture grass on a former 50-year hay farm, which the authors frame as forage production in a managed grassland. It is not natural vegetation, although the paper does not say the grass is currently cut or grazed. It is not E2, because a plant hydraulic and soil water model parameterized with site traits, run hourly for 23 years, validated against measured plant water potential (Methods, p. 7), and used to test a 6 m row-spacing design meets I2(c). This is consistent with the earlier grassland records R0731 and R0843, which were excluded under E2 rather than E1.
I1: is there agricultural production at the PV facility (possibly a desert PV plant)? E2: model or outcome-only?

Section 2.1.1, Study site (p. 3): "Herbs and cash crops, such as Astragali Radix, Bupleurum chinense, Saposhnikovia divaricate, and Medicago sativa, have been planted underneath the PV panels, forming an agricultural–PV system" | Abstract (p. 1): "we developed a novel soil–plant–PV–atmosphere continuum (SPPVAC) model that integrates airflow, heat, and moisture transport processes with vegetation dynamics. The model was validated with field observations and applied to a representative PV site in Zhangjiakou, northern China."

I1 is met: the site, Desheng PV station in Hebei, is a semi-arid station with medicinal herbs and alfalfa planted under the panels, and its control plots are in nearby farmland under 'similar ... crop management' (Section 2.1.2). It is not a desert solar farm without agriculture. It is not E2, because the authors develop a coupled CFD soil–plant–PV–atmosphere model, validate it against field microclimate and soil data (Section 3.1, RMSE and R2 reported), and use it for crop-specific microclimate and biomass prediction, which meets I2(c).
I1 and E3 (and other criteria as applicable) for a Community Land Model (CLM5) simulation of agrivoltaics.

Abstract (p. 1): "we developed a process‐based agrivoltaic model within the Community Land model 5 to assess the impacts of agrivoltaics on water, energy, and carbon cycles. The model was validated using data from agrivoltaic sites in Illinois and Colorado" | Section 3.3, Simulation Experiment Design (p. 7): "After calibration and validation, we performed several single‐point simulations for maize and soybean at SF 2.0, and C3 grass at JSG, each with specific objectives"

I1 is met: the model represents two named agrivoltaic installations with crop production under single-axis trackers (soybean yield was measured at Solar Farm 2.0, and pasture grass grows at Jack's Solar Garden; Section 3.1). It is not E3, because CLM5 is run as single-point simulations at those sites at patch and system level, not as a regional, national, or global potential or suitability map. It meets I2(c) as a calibrated and validated process model used for design (sensitivity to ground coverage ratio), it is a peer-reviewed journal article (I4), and no exclusion applies.
E2: an outcome-only field experiment, or does it build or apply a model or sensing system?

Results (accepted manuscript p. 15): "Using the System Advisor Model (SAM) for a traditional and a co-location PV system in Tucson, AZ, we calculated that temperature reductions in the growing months of May-July from the co-location system lead to a 3% increase in generation" | Methods, Monitoring Equipment & Variables Monitored (accepted manuscript p. 24): "We used the System Advisor Model (SAM) parameterized for Tucson, Arizona, USA, to quantify normal power generation for an example 200 kW DC system [...] The only variable we differed between the adjacent traditional and agrivoltaic installations was PV panel temperature."

This is borderline, so the current decision is kept. The study is mainly a field experiment, and its standard sensors and datalogger would not on their own meet I2(d). However, it does more than report measured outcomes: it applies a computational PV energy model (SAM), driven by the measured agrivoltaic panel temperatures, to estimate electrical yield. This fits I2(c) ('PV energy or electrical yield ... used for estimation') and matches how R1616 and R2860 (field trials plus PVsyst or SAM) were treated. The model step is minor and uses SAM defaults for an example system. Page numbers refer to the DOE public-access accepted manuscript.
E2: an outcome-only field experiment, or does it build or apply a model or sensing system (as for R0349)?

Abstract (p. 1): "Sixty-day-old hibiscus plants were grown in pots for thirty days either beneath photovoltaic (PV) panels or in open conditions, and PV operational parameters were monitored using wireless sensors connected to an Arduino-based data acquisition system." | Materials and methods, Solar PV panel setup (p. 3): "The Arduino microcontroller board (Leonardo with ZigBee Socket Module) receives the sensor output signals and uses the ZigBee wireless sensor network, which is dispersed throughout the PV subsystem monitoring area, to gather and send all data."

This is borderline, so the current decision is kept. The study applies an IoT data-acquisition system for agrivoltaic PV data: current, voltage and temperature sensors feed an Arduino and a ZigBee wireless sensor network, with automatic SQL logging every 20 s (p. 3). That meets the wording of I2(d), 'develops or applies ... IoT, monitoring, data-acquisition ... system', and matches how R0867 was treated. Against this, the system is not developed or evaluated in the paper, the temperature–voltage regression is only descriptive, and on a strict 'develops' reading the study would be E2. There is also an I1 concern: the plants are potted ornamentals purchased from a nursery and kept under a low ground-mounted array for 30 days with no yield, which is close to the R1084 (pollinator plants) precedent. Neither issue is clear enough to change the decision.
I1: is a solar greenhouse with a smart artificial lighting system agrivoltaic (PV and crop production sharing land or structure)?

Abstract: "as a closed agrivoltaic system, the solar greenhouse experiences a problem of optimizing the natural light in generating electricity and producing crops at the same time. The roofing solar modules prevent the plants from receiving adequate amount of sunlight" | Section II.D, Experimental Setup: "There were three solar modules in the setup with the crops placed under the middle PV."

I1 is met: PV modules form the roof of a greenhouse in which romaine lettuce is grown and harvested directly beneath them. This is the 'PV greenhouses or PV-shaded protected cultivation in which plants are grown' case that I1 names, not PV on a building with no plants under it. The rooftop location and small prototype scale do not fail I1 or I3. I2 is met by the IoT monitoring system and the fitted irradiance-to-indoor-light model that controls LED dimming.
I1 and E2 for an optimization of the water-energy-food nexus (charted from the abstract only).

Abstract: "To generate the necessary experimental data for a meaningful case study, a year-long field study was carried out to generate experimental data for three fields were constructed in Kuwait using open-field, agrivoltaic, and greenhouse farming methods." | Abstract: "formulating WEF nexus problems as multi-objective, multi-period optimization problems with data-driven models based on field work [...] An optimization formulation is developed to determine the optimal system configuration, water and energy uses and sources, and crop mix selection."

I1 is met at abstract level: an agrivoltaic field was built and run for a year, and it is one of the candidate farming configurations in the optimization superstructure. The abstract does not describe the agrivoltaic layout, and agrivoltaics is only one option within a wider desalination and energy system, so the judgement rests on the abstract. It is not E2: the study develops data-driven models fitted to field data and a multi-objective, multi-period optimization of configuration, water, energy and crop mix (I2(a) and I2(c)), not an economic-only analysis.
